VI.description: The RemoteVI server: ONE While Loop\2C no event structure (docs\5Carchitecture.md\2C tools\5Cmock-server\5Cserver.mjs). REENTRANT (preallocated clone)\2C so a LabVIEW application instance can run one per port. STRUCTURE\3A before the loop the listener and the stop notifier are created and RemoteVI Loop Init.vi runs Server Setup and returns the context (what does not change while the share runs) and the initial loop state\3B the loop carries four shift registers - the state (one cluster)\2C the clients\2C the pending connections and the error - and each iteration waits for a connection\2C greets and accepts it (RemoteVI Loop Greeting.vi\2C RemoteVI Accept Clients.vi)\2C looks at the target (RemoteVI Track Target.vi\3A flags\2C popups\2C windows\2C geometry\2C panel info) and serves the clients (RemoteVI Serve Clients Step.vi\3A input\2C popups again\2C origin\2C tips\2C splitters\2C overlay\2C frames\2C windows\2C status\2C VI Stopped). The paragraphs below describe what those steps do. share.window not 0 makes it a WINDOW TARGET\3A that window of any process is shared instead of VI's front panel - over VI Server as the VI whose panel it is when its LabVIEW runs one (RemoteVI Server Setup.vi\2C status kind VI Server\3B modifier keys\2C tip strips and splitter bars then run inside that process through RemoteVI Remote Hooks.vi)\2C else (Win32 only - capture\2C input\2C popups\2C other windows of its process\2C its geometry and whether it still exists\3B no tips\2C no splitters\2C no VI Server)\2C so a LabVIEW application instance can run one per port. share holds the access token\2C the net address to listen on (127.0.0.1 for this computer only\2C 0 for the whole network)\2C the link\2C view only and whole network. Before the loop it creates a TCP listener on port at share's net address and sends its error cluster on the notifier <stop notifier name>\3Astarted (RemoteVI Start.vi waits for it\2C so a port in use is reported to the caller)\2C obtains the notifier named stop notifier name and builds the greeting from the name of VI (RemoteVI Greeting.vi). Each iteration\3A ACCEPT - waits at most 5 ms for a connection and hands it to RemoteVI Accept Clients.vi\2C which keeps accepted connections PENDING and reads their request heads with zero-timeout reads\2C serves a complete head (RemoteVI Handle Connection.vi\2C at most 8 WebSocket clients)\2C greets and adds an upgraded connection as a client\2C and drops one that has sent no complete head within 5 s - so an idle connection (a browser's speculative preconnect) never stalls the loop. POPUPS (docs\5Carchitecture.md\2C section Popups) - RemoteVI Track Popups.vi lists the LabVIEW popups (Win32 only - while a popup is open LabVIEW's UI thread is in a modal loop and every VI Server UI call blocks) whenever a client is connected\2C a popup was open last time or the geometry is due\2C hides on the host the popups a remote click opened (within 1 s) and tip strips that can only stem from the remote pointer\2C and gives the modal popups at their LOGICAL positions (real - d). WINDOWS (docs\5Cprotocol.md section 7) - RemoteVI Track Windows.vi lists the application's other windows (dialogs\2C native file dialogs\2C subVI panels\3B Win32 only)\3B while one of them is modal LabVIEW's UI thread runs the dialog's modal loop and the loop makes no VI Server call\2C exactly as while a popup is open. GEOMETRY - the panel geometry and window handle are cached (RemoteVI Get Panel Geometry.vi before the loop\2C then every 500 ms and right after a popup closes - RemoteVI Refresh Geometry.vi - but only while NO popup is open and not within 300 ms of a click). SERVICE - every client is serviced (RemoteVI Service Clients.vi) with the cached geometry\2C handle and popups\3B the displacement d it returns is kept for the next iteration (reset when the last popup closes). SECOND LISTING - after servicing and the hover\2C when a client posted a message that may open a popup or a popup is open\2C RemoteVI Retrack Popups.vi lists the popups once more\2C so a popup the input just opened is hidden on the host at once (layered with alpha 0\2C RemoteVI Hide Remote Popups.vi) and\2C when the popups changed\2C its OVERLAY goes out before this iteration's frame (RemoteVI Send Overlay.vi with period 0). HOVER - RemoteVI Menu Hover.vi applies the remote pointer a client moved over an open LabVIEW menu with keys (the highlight follows it with VK_DOWN / VK_UP\2C VK_RIGHT after 400 ms on an item opens its submenu\2C VK_LEFT closes submenus when the pointer rests on a parent) - no cursor and no menu is moved. SPLITTERS - LabVIEW moves a splitter bar only while it tracks the real mouse\2C so the browser drags the bars itself\3A right after each geometry refresh RemoteVI Read Splitters.vi reads the bars ({LV.Panel} Splitters[]) for the splitters message (a new client gets it with its greeting\2C all clients when it changed)\2C and RemoteVI Apply Splitter.vi sets the Position of the bar a client dropped (s id pos\2C stored by RemoteVI Splitter Request.vi) whenever no popup and no modal window is open\3B after a move the bars and tips are read again and frames come every 16 ms. TIPS - right after each geometry refresh (so never while a popup or a modal window is open) RemoteVI Read Tips.vi reads the tip strips of the panel's controls through VI Server\3B a new client gets the tips message with its greeting and RemoteVI Send Tips.vi tells all clients when it changed (docs\5Cprotocol.md 3.3). ORIGIN - where the panel starts inside the frame (below the menu bar and toolbar) is cached with the geometry\3B a new client gets it with its greeting (RemoteVI Origin Message.vi)\2C and RemoteVI Send Origin.vi tells all clients when it changed. FRAMES - RemoteVI Capture And Send.vi makes a frame at most every 1000/fps ms while a client is connected - every 16 ms while a client posted a click or a key in this iteration or within the last 300 ms (recent click?)\2C so the change it causes reaches the browser at once instead of up to one frame period later - and sends it to each client\3B a frame is the whole window below its title bar (menu bar\2C toolbar\2C panel\2C scrollbars)\2C copied from the window's composited surface (RemoteVI Capture Frame.vi) - no VI Server call\2C so frames keep coming while a popup is open. OTHER WINDOWS - RemoteVI Send Windows.vi sends each client the list (windows [...]) when it changed and\2C in an iteration that made a frame\2C each window's changes as a WINDOW FRAME (seq and flow control shared with FRAME)\3B input goes to the window RemoteVI Route Input.vi picks. OVERLAY - RemoteVI Send Overlay.vi sends the popups as an OVERLAY message when it changed (docs\5Cprotocol.md section 3.2)\3B not in an iteration that made a frame (its period is then 1e9 ms) but in the next one\2C 1 ms later - capturing and PNG-encoding the popups right after the frame made the iteration\2C and with it the frame gap\2C longer (measured). Closed clients are dropped and their connections closed (RemoteVI Drop Closed Clients.vi). While the panel window is disabled (a modal dialog is up\2C even before it is listed - a native file dialog takes a moment to appear) no VI Server call is made either\2C as such a call would wait for the dialog's modal loop\3B for a window of another LabVIEW over VI Server it would block the loop until the dialog closes. The loop stops when the notifier delivers anything\2C when VI is no longer running (RemoteVI VI Stopped.vi\2C once a second while VI Server may be called - so the server ends with your application)\2C or on a listener error other than a timeout. Then every client gets close 1001\2C every connection and the listener are closed and the notifier released\2C and the share's entry is removed from the status (RemoteVI Publish Status.vi\2C which publishes it every 500 ms while the loop runs). Launched asynchronously by RemoteVI Start.vi.
